designPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a NEW character design roster for a top-down pixel-art roguelike called AI VS NAIWA. This is a single concept-sheet image, not an animation atlas yet.

Create sixteen ORIGINAL frog-inspired absurd monsters entirely from imagination. Do not refer to any previously shown or existing game sprite, do not trace or refine earlier designs. Reinvent anatomy, silhouettes, proportions, faces, and palettes. All should feel like one confident, charmingly weird pixel-art game, with the clarity and craft of premium 2D roguelike sprites. Their appeal comes from strong shapes and expressive deadpan faces, NOT realistic detail, ornamental clutter, or grotesque gore.

Composition: exactly 4 rows by 4 columns of equal spacious cells on a fully transparent background. Exactly ONE whole-body creature per cell, fully inside its cell with generous clear space, feet and appendages visible. No labels, lettering, grids, borders, scenery, or drop shadows. Each creature faces 3/4 right, slight top-down view, same light direction upper left. Most creatures roughly 48-64 logical pixels tall, small minion visibly smaller and boss visibly larger. Show clean pixel clusters at integer nearest-neighbor enlargement: deliberate hard square pixel edges, sparse dark outlines, around 8-12 well chosen flat colors per creature, 3-tone material ramps, NO smoothing, NO airbrush, NO gradients, NO glossy 3D rendering, NO noisy dithering, NO vector curves masquerading as pixels.

Design order, left to right row by row:
1. Chase/bite: a low, forward-leaning jade frog with a broad angular lower jaw, tiny close-set eyes, oversized forearms and a cocky slack expression; pear-shaped torso, not a circular ball.
2. Fast scout: a tall narrow pale-mint reed frog with sweeping folded hindlegs and a small pointed head, alert asymmetrical eye brows; dynamic runner silhouette.
3. Heavy tank: a squat slate-blue armored toad enclosed in a broad cracked ceramic-like shell, pale face peeking from under the visor-shaped shell rim, heavy hands and tiny planted feet; organic armor, no metal bucket.
4. Ranged spitter: a plump lavender cheek-pouch frog with ballooned asymmetric cheeks, a tiny pursed mouth and sleepy half-closed eyes; warm cream throat, compact rear legs; no horn or trumpet.
5. Stationary turret: a rooted coral-red frog creature with a wide flat mushroom-like crest and three heavy folded petal feet, cream muzzle with three small firing pores; no flowerpot.
6. Charging enemy: a rust-orange wedge-headed horned frog with swept-back dorsal fins, one short forward forehead horn, muscular shoulders and an irritable squint; low battering-ram silhouette, no bowling ball.
7. Leaping enemy: a butter-yellow frog with extraordinarily broad folded hindlegs and small mitten hands, a narrow oval torso, puffed chest and hopeful vacant expression; no mechanical spring.
8. Splitting enemy: a translucent-looking but flat-color seafoam gelatin frog parent carrying three distinct dark tadpole shapes visibly inside its large belly; soft angular bean silhouette, two side arms, ONE head; no stacked frogs.
9. Tiny minion: a midnight-blue tadpole with an oversized off-center eye and a thin hooked tail, one cream highlight, confused little mouth; no sunglasses.
10. Exploding enemy: a bright salmon inflated puffer-frog with four short triangular side fins, small feet and an embarrassed tiny face, darker stress-stripe cheeks and a cream belly; no bomb, no fuse.
11. Tongue enemy: a deep teal gecko-frog with narrow long head, curled magenta tongue resting around its shoulders like a scarf, large pale lower jaw and tiny skeptical eyes, broad planted hands.
12. Summoner: a pale lilac broad-backed brood frog with a shell-shaped cream cradle on its back holding three small pearl eggs, tired heavy eyelids, one front hand cupping an egg; strong arched silhouette, not a pile of eggs.
13. Burrowing enemy: an ochre mole-toad with a flat shovel-shaped snout, two enormous ivory digging claws, low hood-like forehead and black slit eyes; no miner helmet or lamp.
14. Spinning enemy: a slim periwinkle ribbon-fin frog balancing on one long foot, broad fan-shaped orange tail and flared webbed hands, smug sideways stare; clear spinning-dancer silhouette, no cap, jewelry, or street clothes.
15. Gas enemy: a moss-and-lime squat marsh toad with three hollow reed-like tubes growing from its back, drooping pale cheeks and puffed throat, small solid shapes of pale green vapor directly at the tube tips, sickly amused face.
16. Boss: a new massive warm-ivory milk-toad monarch, broad heavy pear-shaped body with an apron-like cream belly, pale golden shoulders, very short strong legs, two heavy hanging hands, large flat sleepy face with tiny eyes and crooked confident mouth; asymmetrical soft crown-like milk droplet crest, folded dark-caramel back fins. Comedic and formidable, not a humanoid yellow dinosaur, no existing character reference.

The set must be newly designed, coherent, highly readable and appealing. Avoid identical round heads with accessories. Vary body mass, posture, jaw shapes, eye spacing, and negative space.
notes: Approved NEW frog roster; native low resolution and concise keyframes selected by user. Old v1/v2 art was not a reference.

sources.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: simplified 2D pixel game animation source.
Use ONLY the specified character from the attached NEW frog roster as identity reference. Simplify it substantially while preserving its silhouette, defining appendages and main colors. Not the old game's sprites.
Exactly FOUR equal columns and SIX equal rows = TWENTY-FOUR frames of that ONE character on a transparent canvas, aspect ratio 2:3. Each frame in its own equally sized cell, constant anchor, body scale and ground line, generous margins around all sides. Whole character fully inside its cell, no overlapping neighboring poses. No text, labels, numbers, frames, grid, background, ground shadows or external projectiles.
Very coarse clean pixel art: design each creature at about 24-32 logical pixels wide, enlarged by integer nearest-neighbor. Obvious large square pixel steps; 8-12 flat colors; simple green/cream or character-colored masses; ONE pixel outline. Reduce texture, small markings and micro-shading. No gradients, fine stippling, noisy rough edges, smooth illustration or painted antialiasing. Make the face readable with just a few pixels.
Use FEWER but STRONGER hand-drawn key poses, no redundant filler frames and no static-image translation. All poses three-quarter RIGHT except a requested spin row.
Rows left to right:
1. IDLE 4-frame loop: relaxed, breath in, peak breath plus blink, breath out; subtle deformation and appendage movement. End connects to first.
2. WALK 4-frame complete loop: foot contact, passing/compression, opposite contact, opposite passing/rebound. Articulate limbs rather than slide a static body. End connects to first.
3. first 2 cells WINDUP: halfway coiled, fully coiled; last 2 cells ATTACK: most extended attack, contact/follow-through. Follow the character-specific attack below.
4. first 2 cells RECOVER: follow-through settles, neutral; last 2 cells HIT: quick compressed recoil, soft rebound.
5. SPECIAL 4-frame loop as described below; all in place.
6. DEATH 4 frames: startled slump, fallen/collapsed body, small contained colored puff, a tiny speck. Last frame remains minimally nonempty. No gore.
Only 24 frames. Clear simplified character design and strong readable poses are the priorities.
CHARACTER: naiwa_chaser, reference row 1 column 1. Identity: jade green frog with huge forearms, low pear-shaped body, cream wide lower jaw, small sleepy golden eyes.
WALK: heavy alternating quadrupedal gait.
ATTACK: a crouch followed by a wide-mouth forward bite and planted front hands.
SPECIAL ROW: a soft belly-and-jaw chuckle loop.
